courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Food, Fitness, and Health
courses.description: This course introduces undergraduates to evidence-based nutrition and exercise science, empowering them to critically evaluate media claims, explore diverse professional perspectives, and apply practical strategies to promote health in college and beyond.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Introduction to Food Studies: From Science to Society
courses.description: Introduction to food studies covering a variety of topics including how food was consumed over history, land use and aquaculture, food in the arts, food and culture in the American South, food politics, and nutrition science. Previously offered as ANTH 175.

source.text: NUTR 175. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST. | AMST 175 .

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Introduction to Human Nutrition
courses.description: Relationships of human nutrition to health and disease. Integration of biology, chemistry, and social sciences as related to human function. Nutrient composition of foods and safety of the food supply.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Sustainable Local Food Systems: Intersection of Local Foods and Public Health
courses.description: This course examines the health, economic, and environmental impacts of our current food system with a focus on current efforts to build a more local, equitable, and sustainable food system, including looking at systemic racism and its effect on the food system.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Global Sustainable Food Systems
courses.description: This course will provide an overview of global food systems drivers, elements, and activities; key players; key problems, and potential solutions. Students will explore these challenges worldwide, gaining insight into the design, implementation, and impact of programs, policies, and interventions aimed at addressing them.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Nutrition in Action: Applied Service-Learning and Community Engagement
courses.description: This course provides undergraduate nutrition students with the opportunity to integrate their academic study of nutrition with community-based service. Students would get hands-on experience in the field of nutrition and public health as part of this course working with a community-based food or nutrition organization. Students will apply foundational knowledge of nutrition by engaging with community health centers, community gardens, food pantries, non-profit organizations, schools, and/or public health organizations aligned with students' career interests. Through hands-on projects, reflection, and collaboration, students develop practical skills in nutrition education, communication, and program implementation while fostering civic responsibility and cultural awareness.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Undergraduate Research Experience in Nutrition
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. For undergraduates enrolled in the department's baccalaureate degree program. Directed readings or laboratory study on a selected topic. May be taken more than once for credit.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Introduction to Nutritional Biochemistry
courses.description: Function of the human body focusing on chemical properties, function, and metabolism of nutrients. Biochemistry of nutrients with a limited focus on medical aspects of nutrient metabolism. For advanced undergraduates and graduate students needing to enhance background prior to NUTR 600 .

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Fundamentals of Food and Nutrition Policy in Public Health
courses.description: This course focuses on food and nutrition policy on a federal, state, and local level. Topics covered include policy formation, interest/consumer advocacy groups, key legislation, how research informs policy, equity and diversity, global food policy issues, sustainability and health, advocacy, and current public health nutrition policy hot topics and examples.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Foundations of Nutrition Interventions
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce students to clinical trials in nutrition, including experimental designs, nutrition intervention methods, and skills necessary to critically analyze, describe, and evaluate feeding and behavioral nutrition interventions. The course covers concepts, skills and methods related to nutrition interventions, with an emphasis on theory-based interventions at the individual, community, or environmental levels to improve health and nutrition outcomes.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Human Metabolism: Macronutrients
courses.description: Cell biochemistry and physiology emphasizing integration of proteins, carbohydrates, and lipids in whole-body metabolism; regulation of energy expenditure, food intake, metabolic adaptations, and gene expression; and macronutrient-related diseases (atherosclerosis, obesity).

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Food And Your Life Stages
courses.description: This course covers nutrition during the life cycle. Units include women during preconception, pregnancy, and lactation; infancy; childhood; adolescence; and older adults (65+). Nutrient and energy needs, assessment of nutritional status, and cultural and socioeconomic barriers are discussed for each phase.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Human Metabolism: Micronutrients
courses.description: Cell biochemistry and physiology emphasizing metabolism of vitamins and minerals including antioxidant protection, immune function, nutrient control of gene expression, and disease states induced by deficiencies (e.g., iron-deficient anemia).
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, NUTR 400 and 600; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Nutrition Research Seminar
courses.description: The changing landscape of nutritional science research has increased the demand for early-career researchers to be more transdisciplinary, perform highly rigorous research, and be prepared for less-traditional research positions. This course is designed to introduce first-year undergraduate BSPH nutrition students to the foundations of nutrition research. It provides an introduction to nutrition research topics, research methods, study design, research ethics, and the generation and development of research questions within the context of nutrition science. This course also covers aspects of professionalism in public health.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Navigating Culture, Technology, and Communication in Nutrition
courses.description: In the course, students will explore cultural foodways and regional food practices. Students will examine the influence of technology and social media on effective communication and nutrition messaging. Emphasis will be placed on cultural awareness and leveraging digital platforms in nutrition practice. Students will learn how to frame messages for individuals, groups, and broader public audiences.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Mouse Models of Human Disease
courses.description: This course will focus on the laboratory mouse as a model organism to learn fundamental genetic concepts and understand how state-of-the-art experimental approaches are being used to elucidate gene function and the genetic architecture of biological traits.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Food Service Systems Management Experience
courses.description: This is a food service management practicum that applies the basic concepts of institutional food service systems. Two laboratory hours per week.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Honors Research in Nutrition
courses.description: This is an honors course for research for the first semester of senior year, to be followed by NUTR 692H in the second semester. NUTR 691H / 692H is a two-course sequence. Enrollment is only for students approved to conduct a senior honors thesis project.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Honors Research in Nutrition

Committee and faculty research director. A written report is required. May be taken more than once for credit. Six laboratory hours per week.

courses.title: Nutrition Research

courses.title: Readings in Nutrition

courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 8 total completions.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Nutrition Practicum Preparation
courses.description: This course provides support for the practicum process and trains students on how to ethically, meaningfully, and professionally engage and prepare for practicum placements. Students will learn how to work within their organization and their stakeholders through building skills in leadership and interprofessional practice. Additionally, students will sharpen their clinical skills in preparation for their hospital-based experience and include mandatory on-boarding requirements.

courses.title: Human Nutrition
courses.description: Fundamental scientific premises of human nutrition. This course covers the basic concepts of macro and micronutrients, food sources, and the evidence-based requirements for a healthy diet. This course integrates nutritional needs of populations, with an emphasis on nutrition-related diseases, including over and undernutrition.

Nutrient and energy needs, assessment of nutritional status, and cultural and socioeconomic barriers are discussed for each phase.

courses.title: Nutrition Across the Lifecycle
courses.description: This course covers global perspectives on nutrition across the life cycle including US and international food-based recommendations for the following life phases: Adults, Pregnancy and Lactation, Infants and Toddlers, Children and Adolescents, and Older Adults. Heavy emphasis is placed on understanding diet-disease relationships across each life phase as well as opportunities and strategies for intervention using life course and ecological perspectives.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Community Nutrition
courses.description: This course provides graduate students with competencies to assess factors that influence the nutritional status of the population; identify community resources to promote and support nutrition and health; conduct community assets and needs assessments; and design, implement, and evaluate public health nutrition programs.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: International Nutrition
courses.description: Provides a broad overview of international nutrition research issues, programs, and policies. Topics will include micronutrient deficiencies, child feeding and growth, determinants of under- and over-nutrition, chronic disease and nutrition, food fortification and supplementation, and nutrition intervention programs and policy.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Taxes, Bans & Burgers: Directed Readings in Global Food Policy
courses.description: Course will explore the social, historical, and political context of how individuals make decisions about what to eat; how this context shapes food policy; and how these policies in turn shape individual behavior, by employing a comparative framework over three countries (China, Mexico, and the U.S.).

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Global Food and Nutrition Security
courses.description: Introduces the basic principles of food and nutrition security from a global lens; addresses nutrition in emergencies and humanitarian contexts; and the role that nutrition security plays in improving the health and well being of populations. Aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills required to conduct population and community-based nutrition research, to assess the food and nutrition security status of vulnerable population groups. Will cover key aspects related to food security interventions, taking into consideration cultural, social, geo-political and environmental dimensions in conflict- affected settings and humanitarian contexts, with a focus on the Middle East and North Africa.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: mHealth for Behavior Change
courses.description: This special topics seminar examines the impact and potential of mobile health interventions and apps for health behavior change. The overall course objective is to understand state of the science and future potential to leverage mobile phones and wearable technologies in innovative and powerful behavior change interventions to improve health. The course considers adaptation of eHealth interventions for mobile delivery, unique opportunities with mHealth, data collection via mobile devices and sensors, and using the data.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Global Healthy And Sustainable Food Systems
courses.description: This course will provide an overview of global food systems drivers, elements, and activities; key players; key problems, and potential solutions. Students will explore these challenges worldwide, gaining insight into the design, implementation, and impact of programs, policies, and interventions aimed at addressing them.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Local Food Systems, Health, and the Environment
courses.description: This course addresses how our current food system impacts the health of people, communities, and the environment. Students will hear from experts across these domains and review the current literature about evidence-based approaches to address the major challenges. Students will learn how to assist local food system partners on how to promote a healthier and sustainable food system. Students may enroll in a 3 credit or 1 credit option.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Nutrition and Cancer: Insights for Prevention and Treatment
courses.description: This course covers emerging research on the interplay of nutrition, physical activity and cancer from a multidisciplinary perspective. Students will gain a solid scientific basis to better weigh and interpret the information available on nutrition and cancer while further developing skills in presenting and discussing emerging research focused on the links between cancer and a range of diet-related exposures (including obesity, micronutrients, dietary patterns, meat intake, coffee consumption, dietary supplements, and alcohol) and physical activity in relation to the development, progression, treatment and survivorship of the most common types of cancer.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Food Science
courses.description: Introduction to foods, chemical and physical properties, nutritional composition, food safety, production, and regulation.

source.text: NUTR 760. | 2 Credits. | Corequisite, NUTR 761L or NUTR 760L .

courses.title: Food Science Laboratory
courses.description: Basic culinary techniques. Classes illustrate biochemical processes and food properties covered in lecture. Introduction to new foods and food ideas. Critical evaluation of recipes. Laboratory fee required. Three laboratory hours per week.

courses.description: This course introduces basic methods of dietary assessment, reviews various topics in nutrition epidemiology, and teaches the skills needed for critical evaluation of the nutritional epidemiologic literature.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Nutrition Policy
courses.description: This course focuses on food and nutrition policy on federal, state, local, and organizational levels. Topics covered include legislative and regulatory processes, policy evaluation, advocacy, agencies/organizations involved with food and nutrition policy/advocacy, how research informs policy, and ways to engage with food and nutrition policy/advocacy efforts. Key food and nutrition-related legislation and current public health nutrition policy examples from the US and globally will be discussed. Permission of the instructor for undergraduates.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Global Cardiometabolic Disease Seminar
courses.description: This core seminar addresses biology, genetics, epidemiology, intervention and policy strategies relevant for addressing global cardiometabolic disease, as well as, professional development and responsible conduct of research in global settings.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Physical Activity Epidemiology and Public Health
courses.description: This course provides an overview of major issues in physical activity measurements, population distribution, correlates, impacts (physically and economically), and public health recommendations. Interventions, including relevant theories, will be reviewed. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Introduction to Obesity: Cell to Society
courses.description: Provides a broad survey of obesity research including measurement issues, biological, social and economic etiologies, health and economic consequences, and prevention and treatment of obesity.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Doctoral Seminar
courses.description: The changing landscape of nutritional science research has increased the demand of early-career investigators to be more transdisciplinary, perform highly rigorous research, and be prepared for less-traditional research positions. With a framework of performing reproducible research, this course introduces students to the concepts and skills to perform and understand rigorous nutrition research. The course also covers aspects of research ethics, effective use of UNC research resources, work-life balance and research innovation.
